# BTC Heirloom — Bitcoin Self-Custody & Inheritance Scheme

> A vendor-free, trust-minimized playbook for long-term Bitcoin self-custody and
> posthumous inheritance. Core idea: replace trust with physical distribution and
> single points of failure with incomplete secrets. Security does not depend on
> secrecy (Kerckhoffs's principle). Contains no real keys, addresses, or locations.

- License: CC BY-SA 4.0
- Language: Chinese docs (with English README summary)

## What this is
An executable operational playbook (process, checklists, threat model) for an
individual's Bitcoin custody and inheritance. It is NOT wallet software and
contains no code or keys.

## Key documents
- docs/01-生前流程.md — setup, daily spending, vault distribution, annual drill
- docs/02-身后流程.md — heir's step-by-step recovery guide
- docs/03-威胁模型.md — threat model, trust assumptions, attacker profiles
- docs/04-执行清单.md — shopping list, setup checklist, verification steps
- docs/05-登记App配合.md — how a local encrypted registry fits in (product-agnostic)
- docs/06-FAQ.md — questions and direct answers
- docs/07-multisig升级路径.md — optional 2-of-3 multisig upgrade path
- docs/08-费用清单.md — cost breakdown

## Core design (30 seconds)
Three artifact classes, each stored in three separate places, mutually isolated:
1. Seed material (steel plate / SeedQR) — home safe / bank safe-deposit box / family home
2. Vault password (machine-generated, 14+ chars) — relative A / relative B / lawyer
3. Vault file (encrypted bundle: BIP39 passphrase + locations + tutorial) —
   family phones / bank·lawyer backup / blind copy at a relative's

Iron rule: seed material and the vault password never co-locate. No single
compromised location yields a complete wallet.

While alive: watch-only wallet + air-gapped QR signer + memorized BIP39 passphrase.
After death: heirs retrieve the password → decrypt the vault → retrieve the seed →
recover in any BIP39 wallet.

## Direct answers
- Is it a wallet? No — a playbook; no code, no keys.
- Does publishing it weaken it? No — security is not in the secrecy of the method.
- Multisig? Optional 2-of-3 upgrade path in docs/07.
- Forgotten BIP39 passphrase? Unrecoverable by design; mitigate with annual drills.
- Dependency on any app or vendor? None — recovery uses open standards (BIP39) and
  a documented .vault format.
